item.title: Does Lufthansa Group Still Have a Lufthansa Problem?
item.description: The Lufthansa Group has plenty of bright spots. Sadly, the airline bearing its name isn’t always one of them.

item.title: Etihad Rail Would Cut Abu Dhabi–Dubai Trips to One Hour and Connect 11 Cities
item.description: The project’s adoption will depend on whether the ticket price is affordable to the daily commuter.

item.title: The Taj Built Indian Hotels Company. Ginger Is the Growth Engine
item.description: While Taj still defines Indian Hotels Company's identity, the future growth of the hotel company may depend less on palaces and more on platforms.

item.title: Tripadvisor Sees Traffic Decline from AI Overviews, Considers ‘Strategic Alternatives’ (Again)
item.description: Tripadvisor has borne the brunt of declining SEO traffic from Google for many years. Now AI Overviews are pinching Tripadvisor even harder.

item.title: Sabre, PayPal, and Mindtrip Partner on Agentic AI Travel Booking
item.description: Google just got a run for its money: Sabre, PayPal, and Mindtrip join forces to let travelers plan and book trips inside AI chats. If it works, it’s another sign the next distribution shift may come from travel’s own stack, not just Big Tech.

item.title: Hyatt Targets 90% Asset-Light Business, Plans More Hotel Sales
item.description: Hyatt’s real estate sell-off is largely complete. The focus now shifts from asset sales to sustaining fee growth.

item.title: Spirit Airlines Brings Back 500 Furloughed Flight Attendants, Will Sell Off Aircraft
item.description: Right before spring break, Spirit is bringing back some flight attendants to work after furloughing around 1,800 flight attendants last year.

item.title: Hyatt CEO Sees Lift From AI Search; Reveals ChatGPT App
item.description: Hotel groups are increasingly sharing AI risks openly. But Hyatt and others have no choice but to keep experimenting.

item.title: Chesky Disses Rivals’ Chatbots — Calls Airbnb’s AI ‘Impossible to Replicate’
item.description: In an era when speed to market is a given, Chesky is arguing that nice and easy does it will win the day. It would be better to say, "We are behind in our AI development, but we are confident that we will get to where we need to be."

item.title: Expedia’s B2B Surge Buys Time for Vrbo and Hotels.com
item.description: Expedia's B2B division is growing nearly five times faster than its consumer brands. That gap buys time for the Vrbo and Hotels.com turnaround — but 2026 will test whether efficiency gains can translate into sustained momentum.
